subject: Capacity snapshot + provisional hold request for Meridian POC
messages:
From: Alex Cho <alex.cho@meridianai.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@meridianai.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC resource ask — rough numbers and provisional hold request

Evelyn — thanks again for the demo last week. Meridian's engineering team finished the performance estimate and we want to align on capacity needs for the late-stage POC (target start: 2026-07-05). High level: 6 concurrent heavy-generation workers (approx. 32–48 tokens/s sustained each), peak QPS ~120, and long context runs up to 32k tokens. Our initial ask is for a provisional hold on the equivalent of 6x 80GB-class GPUs (A100/80GB profile) for an 8-week runway while we finalize purchase/commitment.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provision and soft-reserve that footprint in us-west-2, and if there are constraints on hard/soft holds for that duration? Attaching a one-pager that summarizes the workload.

Appreciate a quick capacity snapshot and next steps.

— Alex
Alex Cho
Head of Infrastructure, Meridian AI
Attachments: meridian_poc_requirements.pdf (1 page summary)

Subject: Re: POC resource ask — rough numbers and provisional hold request

Alex — thanks, received the one-pager. We can do a preliminary ops check but need to validate a couple of items before committing a soft hold: exact concurrent slot sizing (workers vs. inference pool), expected tokens per request distribution, and whether you can accept a quantized/residual fallback if 80GB native SKUs are constrained.

Ben / Rishi — can you run a capacity snapshot for us-west-2 and call out: current 80GB-equivalent free headroom, existing pending holds expiring in June/July, and whether we can support an 8-week provisional hold without impacting committed customers? I’ve attached the Meridian one-pager for context.

Next steps (sales + ops):
- Ops: snapshot + recommended provisional hold length (30/60/8-week options)
- Sales: confirm billing cadence and whether Meridian is willing to accept fallback variants
- Legal: if ops recommends a hard hold, loop legal for SLA/termination terms

Evelyn Hart

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 16:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: POC resource ask — ops check request

Team — did a pool sweep and spoke to capacity planning. Summary: 

- Us-west-2 current free headroom (80GB-equivalent): 4 nodes that can provide 80GB-class performance natively, plus capacity to flex another 4 by combining 40GB nodes with aggressive KV/prefix caching and quantized runtime (not native 80GB perf).
- Pending holds/commits: two existing soft holds (expiring 2026-06-25 and 2026-07-10) that would free up 2x 80GB-equivalent if they are not renewed.
- Thermal/maintenance: scheduled maintenance 2026-06-20 to 2026-06-22 that will reduce available peak slots by ~10% for that window.
- Hard-hard reservation policy: we can approve a 30-day hard hold (billable) without displacing committed customers; a soft hold (non-billable tentative hold) for up to 8 weeks can be recorded but it is subject to bump for higher-priority committed contracts.

Recommendation: propose a 30-day hard hold (billing starts at hold activation) + 30-day soft extension we can honor if we don’t commit those freed up nodes elsewhere. Operational caveat: if Meridian requires guaranteed uninterrupted 6x80GB native for 8 weeks, we would need a signed reserved capacity commit (monthly) or offer a mixed deployment: 4x native 80GB + 2x quantized fallback nodes with auto-failover.

Attachments: capacity_runbook_v2.xlsx (capacity mapping and node list).

Action items: 
- Sales (Evelyn / Ben): confirm whether Meridian accepts mixed provisioning or prefers strict 80GB native (we need answer to model fallback).
- Ops (Monica): if sales asks for a hard hold, provide a hold activation date and invoice cadence to finance.
- Legal: if the customer requires 8-week guaranteed hard reservation, escalate to legal for SLA addendum.

— Monica
Monica Patel
Principal, Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC resource ask — capacity snapshot and provisional hold

Alex — quick update from ops: we can only guarantee 4x native 80GB nodes immediately. We can offer a 30-day billable hard hold for 4x 80GB plus a soft 30-day extension and 2x quantized fallback nodes to reach your target headroom. There is a maintenance window 6/20–6/22 to keep in mind.

If Meridian is comfortable with the mixed plan, we will:
- Activate a 30-day hard hold starting on the date you confirm and issue the invoice for the hold period,
- Record the 30-day soft extension in our backlog (non-billable) while you finalize commitment,
- Provide a runbook (attached) that maps the fallback behavior and failover thresholds.

Please let us know by EOD tomorrow — if you need an uninterrupted 6x80GB native hold for 8 weeks we’ll need a reserved capacity contract (drafted by legal/finance).

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
